author: Mark Atwood
text:
Resolved in collaborative session 2026-05-12.

DECISION RECORD

Textual forms: Both Mastodon-style `@user@host` AND DID URI forms (e.g., `@did:web:alice.example`) are recognized composer-side. Multiple textual forms can coexist; the wire format is the same for all.

Wire form: Reuse `type: "user"` from fig9.1's Mention type discriminator. The `id` field carries the full identifier as known to the authoritative server. No new mention type value; no separate field for federated mentions. The existing Mention shape from fig9.1 D1 already handles this (the id field is opaque).

Resolution: Deployment-defined. Both the parsing (textual form -> candidate id) and the resolution (candidate id -> known ChatContact) are out of spec scope. Server-side validation of the resulting Mention is unchanged (offset/length bounds, ChatContact existence).

Same principle applies to rich-body 'mention' spans (which carry userId): the spec describes the wire field; deployments handle composer-side parsing and resolution.

Implementation: single paragraph added to the Mention section in main draft after the existing field definitions (commit forthcoming). No change to fig9.1 design; no change to the Mention object shape; no new capability or method.

Compatibility:
- fig9.1 unchanged (Mention type discriminator already supports this via type='user' + opaque id)
- q15f reinforced (DID URIs as identifier form is already accommodated by the prose at line ~140, commit 48b6a31)
- 8sgn unaffected (DID resolution/auth mechanics still optional and live in the companion draft)
- f13f's blocker on fig9 is now satisfied (fig9.1 design done)

Closing as resolved. The epic's listed scope was '4 questions' all of which collapse to 'deployment-defined' or 'reuse existing wire shape'. No further child beads needed.
